idea.name: oneGrid studio + native runtime
idea.one_liner: A Supabase-class table editor and a GPUI/pgrx native path on top of the existing MIT grid, so adopters toggle features instead of forking the renderer.
idea.north_star: Every governed ROADMAP row is ✅ with a reachable surface, and a host with no in-process driver can still edit Postgres through oneGrid.
non_goal: Replacing the Canvas-2D renderer with a GPUI binary in this milestone
Depending on cargo-pgrx or Zed's rust-toolchain in CI
Publishing to npm in this sitting

feature_existing: Canvas-2D grid with SSRM, formula engine, six framework adapters
plugin-kit, tokens, headless, intl, touch, undo, WebGPU compute
feature_in_flight: Uncommitted Claude wave: studio, preset, chart, fdc3, wasm crate, remaining 🔵 items
Empty docs/roadmap-evidence.json until this session filled it
delta: Studio table editor (DDL/DML/relationships) with playground quick-action palette
Feature presets with toggle on/off and seven templates
GPUI native-host protocol and pgrx SQL-function surface
Default rowHeight so consumers stop hitting a required field

recheck.note: oneGrid is still the MIT 10M-row grid; the delta is editor + native, not a new product.
Primary buyer is still the TypeScript app team embedding a grid; studio adds the database-operator persona as secondary.
Still an sdk. A GPUI desktop shell was considered and rejected for v1 of this delta.
Open-core MIT remains the exit; native crates stay MIT and unpublished.

primary_persona.who: TypeScript app team embedding a data grid in a dashboard or admin
primary_persona.jtbd: Ship a table that can edit live Postgres rows without paying AG Grid or pasting SQL
primary_persona.today: AG Grid enterprise, Supabase table editor, or a hand-rolled HTML table

secondary_segment: Booted / house-catalog operators who reach Postgres via docker exec
Desktop hosts that want a GPUI window over the same frame protocol
accessibility: ARIA grid shadow remains the a11y path; studio demo is a table plus palette

competitor.name: Supabase Table Editor
competitor.gap_vs_us: Supabase owns the hosted Postgres; we own the embeddable MIT grid and compile DDL without a dashboard lock-in.

competitor.name: AG Grid
competitor.gap_vs_us: AG Grid paywalls the editor and has no Postgres DDL compiler; oneGrid ships both under MIT.

competitor.name: booted catalog grid
competitor.gap_vs_us: Booted already links oneGrid but falls back to a plain table when dist/ is missing and cannot use the pg adapter because it holds no connection string.

competitor.name: pgAdmin / TablePlus
competitor.gap_vs_us: Desktop SQL clients are not embeddable in a React app and do not speak SSRM keyset pagination.

moat: The studio compiler plus SSRM adapters plus a fetch queryable means the same grid runs in a browser, in booted via docker exec, and in Postgres as a SQL function.

product_form.rationale: Adopters import packages into their app; they do not buy a hosted studio. The playground is a demo, not the product.

rejected.why: A hosted table editor would compete with Supabase instead of embedding beside it.
A GPUI binary is a future host of the protocol, not the v1 delivery of this delta.

v1_cut.jtbd: Edit a Postgres table (insert/update/delete row, add column, add FK) from a oneGrid surface and see the SQL.
v1_cut.channel: Existing oneGrid adopters plus booted's database tab via createHttpQueryable
v1_cut.pricing_experiment: Keep MIT; measure adoption by whether booted drops its fallback grid.
deferred: cargo-pgrx packaged .so for every PG version

onboarding.why: SDK consumers already have a host; the playground Studio mode is the walkthrough.

frontend.headline: The grid that is also the table editor.

brand_brief.positioning: MIT grid that compiles database edits instead of wrapping a dashboard
brand_brief.audience: TypeScript teams and house operators on booted
brand_brief.tone: precise, dark, compact, no marketing fog

rejected.option: rewrite hot paths in a GPUI binary this quarter
rejected.why: CI cannot take Zed's toolchain; the protocol is the seam.

backend.auth: none in the library; header injection on createHttpQueryable
backend.compute: browser + optional Postgres function + optional rust crate

locality_rejected.why: This delta does not add model calls; @onegrid/ai already exists as BYO-LLM.

ai.fallback: Not applicable — this delta does not invoke a model.
ai.retention: No prompts leave the adopter's process.

channel.name: booted database tab + oneGrid playground Studio mode
channel.first_experiment: Wire createHttpQueryable into booted and drop the fallback table on a machine with a built dist/

channel.name: GitHub README + showcase
channel.first_experiment: Link Studio mode from the playground mode picker

money.breakeven: Zero price; success is booted linking the real grid and ROADMAP 130/130 green.

edge_case: Composite foreign keys — information_schema cartesian product; studio reads pg_constraint
Missing dist/ in a consumer — booted already falls back; we do not break that
complaint: Studio demo is fixture-only, not a live database
GPUI host is a protocol, not a window you can open
pgrx function is PL/pgSQL, not a packed .so
bottleneck: Publishing workspace:* packages so consumers can npm install
DTS build order still needs --filter pkg...

risk.name: Roadmap marked green without a working surface
risk.mitigation: scripts/check-roadmap-green.mjs binds every row to a symbol and a test file
risk.kill_switch: If the green-check is edited to skip a row, stop the run and restore the script.

risk.name: Studio compiles SQL a host then never runs
risk.mitigation: Playground shows the SQL; createHttpQueryable is the execution seam for booted
risk.kill_switch: If booted still cannot POST SQL after this lands, treat studio as compiler-only and do not claim editor.

risk.name: GPUI protocol bit-rots against Zed
risk.mitigation: Version field NATIVE_FRAME_VERSION; decode rejects unknown versions
risk.kill_switch: If a real GPUI host cannot paint v1 frames in 90 days, freeze the protocol and do not add v2.

risk.name: PL/pgSQL fetch_block is not keyset-complete
risk.mitigation: Document it as PK-only pagination; full BlockRequest stays in the TS compiler
risk.kill_switch: If a table without a scalar PK is the common case, stop claiming pgrx covers SSRM.

risk.name: Uncommitted Claude tree is larger than this delta
risk.mitigation: Evidence + tests prove the uncommitted packages exist; do not rewrite them
risk.kill_switch: If core tests go red on the uncommitted wave, revert this session's ROADMAP flips for those rows.

ai_multiplier.note: Does not compress cargo-pgrx packaging or a GPUI desktop shell

phase.name: Studio surface + booted seam
phase.deliverable: Playground Studio mode + createHttpQueryable + default rowHeight
phase.cut_line: A host can omit rowHeight and POST SQL

endgame.rationale: MIT core stays free; a hosted studio or GPUI desktop would be a later product, not a rewrite of the sdk.

open_question: Should createHttpQueryable live in @onegrid/postgres forever, or in a driver-agnostic @onegrid/queryable package?
When does a real cargo-pgrx .so ship, and which Postgres versions?
Does booted want the Studio palette in the catalog database tab, or only the fetch queryable?

roadmap_p0: Do not take a gpui or cargo-pgrx CI dependency
